itinerary.cal: Most parties climb it snow-covered (winter-spring) to bury the boulder-field gaps and suppress brush; summer ascents are viable but noticeably slower and brushier.

days.note: A single long day: steep, forested trail to Lake Serene (past Bridal Veil Falls), then off-trail through a boulder field above the lake and up easy west-ridge slopes to the flat, wooded (viewless) summit. Real trip-report splits put the trail portion to Lake Serene at ~1h50m and the ridge/summit push at ~2h50m from the lake, with car-to-car totals of 6-9+ hours depending on brush (summer) or snow depth/consolidation (winter-spring).

itinerary.totalNote: A single car-to-car day, roughly 8-8.5 hours for a fit party (range 6-9+ hrs depending on brush/snow), ~11 miles round trip and ~3,650 ft gain — no camp, no permit.

before.descent_text: This is a walk-off/scramble-down, not a rappelling route — no fixed anchors or rope work are used on the standard line. Reverse the ascent line exactly: off the summit, follow the ridge north back to the 5,800 ft saddle, then descend north-northwest off the ridge to the small tarn/bench at 5,200 ft, staying well back from any cornice edge if there is snow. From the tarn, drop back down the open slopes and skirt the cliff bands on the lake (west) side of the ridge as before, downclimbing the short rock band around 3,700 ft with care (the single spot on this route with real exposure), then pick up the Rainy Creek climbers' path back down through the brush to the Pratt Connector Trail and out to the Middle Fork Trailhead. Descent time is roughly 5 hours (about 1.5 hours from summit to Rainy Lake, 2+ hours from the lake back to the car), reflecting the loose talus, brush, and route-finding on the way down being as slow as the way up. Descent-specific hazards: the mossy slab and rock band near 3,700 ft are more consequential to downclimb than to ascend and are the likeliest spot for a slip; the boot path is easy to lose in failing light or fog since it's unofficial and unmarked; and in early/mid season, lingering snow on the upper slopes plus possible cornicing on the summit ridge call for caution and, if conditions warrant, an ice axe.

pitch_detail.notes: Climb the left-side chimney between two prominent V-shaped features on the south face; move left atop the chimney onto knobby terrain to belay.
Sustained knobby face, slabs, and cracks up toward a gully/chimney system; route-finding is somewhat ambiguous through this stretch on the way to Snafflehound Ledge.
Traverse right across the obvious Snafflehound Ledge to a small tree, then a short steep step to the base of the crux pitch.
Route crux: a shallow left-facing dihedral forces you right until an overhang forces a step-across left into a flaring jam crack; eases above the bulge on face holds and chicken-heads.
Crack system/steep gully bypassing a chockstone on the left to the small notch east of the summit horn; watch for loose blocks in the gully.

Delicate friction traverse on a ramp finishing on a good jam crack to the summit; a harder 5.10a thin-hands splitter variant climbs straight out of the notch for parties wanting more technical finish.

before.approach: From the Stuart Lake Trailhead (3,600 ft) at the end of FS Road 7601, follow the Stuart Lake Trail about 2.5 miles to the signed Colchuck Lake Trail (#1599A) junction. Turn right, cross Mountaineer Creek (a rock-hop/log crossing and the last reliable, easy water source for a while), and switchback up 1.6 miles through forest to Colchuck Lake (5,570 ft) — roughly 4.1 miles and 2,000 ft from the car. Boulder-hop along the lake's east shore to the boulder field at its south end (about 5.5 miles in, 2,500 ft gained), then pick up the climbers' trail/talus leading to the base of Aasgard Pass. Aasgard Pass itself gains about 2,000 ft in only 1.25 miles of steep, loose dirt and scree — physically the crux of the approach. It's cairned when snow-free, but in early season (often into July) snow can bridge a hidden creek/moat on the left side of the gully that has caused serious injuries and at least one fatality when climbers post-holed or glissaded into it; the slope is also avalanche-prone with a spring/early-summer snowpack. From the top of the pass (7,841 ft) descend gently into the upper Core basin past Isolation/Tranquil Lake, then continue cross-country roughly 1–1.5 miles north over granite slabs and heather benches toward Prusik Pass and Gnome Tarn (~7,800–8,000 ft); Prusik's south face and the Solid Gold start are about 15–20 minutes from a Gnome Tarn camp. Total is roughly 7.5–8 miles and 4,600 ft one-way from the trailhead. Overnight camping in the Core Zone requires an Enchantments lottery/walk-up permit, so many parties either link the whole climb car-to-car in a long day or secure a permit to camp at Gnome Tarn. When the Stuart Lake/Colchuck approach or Aasgard Pass is closed (wildfire, avalanche danger), the Snow Lakes Trail is a much longer (9+ miles one-way) but lower-angle alternative that eventually requires cross-country travel past Lake Viviane to reach the same south-face base.

schedule.detail: ~20-30 min hike/scramble to the base of the West Ridge

schedule.label: Start climbing
schedule.detail: Low 5th-class ridge, often simulclimbed by competent parties

schedule.label: Reach the summit
schedule.detail: ~1.5 hrs of climbing for a moving party

schedule.label: Begin the descent
schedule.detail: Downclimb/rappel the ridge back toward the notch

schedule.label: Back at camp
schedule.detail: Rest of the day free to explore the Enchantments basin

days.objective: Summit via the West Ridge (5.7, II, 4 pitches)

days.note: Break camp, climb back up to Aasgard Pass, then descend the long way back past Colchuck Lake to the trailhead. Efficient parties sometimes skip this third day and hike all the way out the same evening after climbing, making it a 2-day trip.
days.title: Hike out via Aasgard Pass
days.objective: Return to the Stuart Lake trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A relaxed 3-day trip (~20.5 mi, ~4,700 ft round-trip) built around a quick, popular 4-pitch 5.7 climb; strong parties without a permit often compress it into one ~15-16 hr car-to-car day instead.

before.descent: Descend via the standard West Ridge downclimb/rappels toward the Enchantments basin.

itinerary.cal: Core Enchantments overnight permits are competitive; fit parties without one sometimes push the whole route car-to-car in ~20-24 hrs instead.

days.note: Hike past Colchuck Lake and up Aasgard Pass into the core Enchantments, passing Tranquil, Isolation, and Perfection Lakes. Camp at Gnome Tarn, close to the south face.
days.title: Approach to Gnome Tarn camp

days.note: Chimneys and corner systems for 6 pitches (~650 ft); pitches 1-2 and 3-4 link easily with a 60m rope. Car-to-car parties log about 5.5 hrs of pure climbing, then descend via the standard West Ridge downclimb/rappels.
days.title: Climb the South Face (Burgner-Stanley)

schedule.label: Leave camp
schedule.detail: ~15-20 min to the base of the south face

schedule.label: Start climbing
schedule.detail: P1 chimney or crack (5.7-5.8+) to a tree belay

schedule.label: Continue P2-P5
schedule.detail: Corner systems and a chockstone chimney (5.8-5.9)

schedule.label: Top out
schedule.detail: P6 strenuous crack/corner to the summit; ~5.5 hrs of climbing typical

schedule.label: Descend
schedule.detail: Downclimb/rappel the West Ridge back toward the notch

days.note: Break camp and hike back out over Aasgard Pass and past Colchuck Lake to the trailhead.
days.title: Hike out

itinerary.totalNote: A 3-day trip (~19.5 mi, ~4,500 ft round-trip) around Prusik's classic 6-pitch 5.9+ south-face line, descending via the West Ridge.

before.descent_text: Walk east from the summit and begin the north-face rappel line on slung belay stations — natural anchors (blocks/chockstones with webbing/tat); there's little to no fixed gear at the top. Plan on 3–4 single-rope rappels, most around 25–30m, though the line can also be run with two ropes for fewer, longer rappels. Figure roughly an hour from the summit back to the base if the rap line isn't backed up with other parties, which does happen since several south-face routes share this descent. Bring extra tat to back up aged webbing on the natural anchors.
before.rappel_count_note: Reported as 3-4 single-rope rappels depending on party choices; some parties run the same line with two ropes for fewer, longer rappels. Shared north-side descent used by multiple South Face routes on Prusik Peak, so expect traffic/queuing.
